breakdown.description: The prompt splits the applied torque between the two stepped segments as if they were parallel torsional members, but segments connected in series carry the same internal torque.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly splits the 300,000 N·mm torque between the two segments (95,700 N·mm to AB and 204,300 N·mm to BC), treating them as parallel members. The ground truth requires that both series segments carry the full 300,000 N·mm internal torque. The agent repeated the original error rather than correcting it.

breakdown.description: The torque-sharing rule used in the prompt is a parallel-member compatibility idea, not the correct series-shaft equilibrium relation.
breakdown.reason: The agent applied the parallel-member torsional stiffness proportioning rule to distribute torque, which is the incorrect compatibility-based approach for parallel systems. For series-connected segments, equilibrium dictates the same torque throughout. The agent failed to correct this and instead used the flawed torque-sharing rule from the incomplete prompt.
